counterexample.note: Tick 100 is initialized, but its net liquidity is 0, so the repair skips it. The liquidity total still comes out right because the net is 0. But an initialized tick inside the range is missing, while zero-net ticks below the start are still returned. The hook uses every returned tick to update rewardGrowthOutsideX128, so the share of the tax earned by the [100, 110) position goes to the [90, 100) position instead.

summary: Keeps the start tick when its net liquidity is not zero and otherwise calls _advanceToNextDown. An initialized start tick whose net liquidity is zero is still skipped.
